from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Imagine two blocks sliding on a frictionless floor.",
            "A wall sits on the far left side.",
            "A large block collides with a stationary small block.",
            "We count every collision between blocks and the wall.",
            "Watch as the collision count reveals digits of Pi."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Setup: A Curious Experiment", lecture_lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # Floor
        floor = Line(self.grid["E1"] + LEFT*0.5, self.grid["E6"] + RIGHT*0.5, color=WHITE)
        
        # Small block 'm'
        small_block = Square(side_length=0.4, color="#00FF00", fill_opacity=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(small_block, "E2")
        small_label = MathTex("m", color="#00FF00").scale(0.8)
        small_label.next_to(small_block, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        # Large block 'M'
        large_block = Square(side_length=0.8, color="#0000FF", fill_opacity=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(large_block, "E5")
        large_label = MathTex("M", color="#0000FF").scale(0.8)
        large_label.next_to(large_block, UP, buff=0.1)

        self.play(Create(floor), Create(small_block), Write(small_label), Create(large_block), Write(large_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        # Wall
        wall = Line(self.grid["C1"] + LEFT*0.5, self.grid["E1"] + LEFT*0.5 + DOWN*0.2, color="#FFFFFF", stroke_width=6)
        self.play(Create(wall))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        # Move large block toward small block
        target_pos = self.grid["E3"]
        self.play(
            large_block.animate.move_to(target_pos),
            large_label.animate.next_to(target_pos, UP, buff=0.1),
            run_time=2,
            rate_func=linear
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        # Counter appears
        counter_label = Text("Collisions:", font_size=24, color="#FFFF00")
        self.place_at_grid(counter_label, "A3")
        counter_val = Integer(0, color="#FFFF00")
        counter_val.next_to(counter_label, RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        
        self.play(Write(counter_label), Write(counter_val))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        # Flash numbers 3, 31, 314
        for val in [3, 31, 314]:
            self.play(
                counter_val.animate.set_value(val),
                Flash(counter_val, color="#FFFF00", flash_radius=0.3),
                run_time=1
            )
            self.wait(0.5)

        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data from storyboard
        title = "Prerequisite Knowledge: The Laws of the Game"
        lines = [
            "Energy conservation keeps the system's total speed restricted.",
            "Momentum conservation governs how velocity transfers between blocks.",
            "These physical laws define the rules of every hit."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors
        GREEN = "#00FF00"
        BLUE = "#0000FF"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display 'Energy Conservation' in green (#00FF00) and 'Momentum Conservation' in blue (#0000FF) at the top
        energy_label = Text("Energy Conservation", color=GREEN, font_size=24)
        momentum_label = Text("Momentum Conservation", color=BLUE, font_size=24)
        
        self.place_in_area(energy_label, "A1", "A3", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_in_area(momentum_label, "A4", "A6", scale_factor=0.8)

        self.lecture[0].set_color(GREEN)
        self.play(FadeIn(energy_label), FadeIn(momentum_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Show a pulsing battery icon (#00FF00) in the center
        # Creating a battery icon
        battery_body = Rectangle(width=1.5, height=0.8, color=GREEN, stroke_width=4)
        battery_tip = Rectangle(width=0.2, height=0.4, color=GREEN, fill_opacity=1).next_to(battery_body, RIGHT, buff=0)
        battery_fill = Rectangle(width=1.2, height=0.6, fill_color=GREEN, fill_opacity=0.8, stroke_width=0).move_to(battery_body)
        battery = VGroup(battery_body, battery_tip, battery_fill)
        
        self.place_in_area(battery, "B3", "D4", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Pulse mechanism using ValueTracker
        pulse_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        def pulse_updater(m):
            # Scale factor oscillating between 0.95 and 1.05
            val = pulse_tracker.get_value()
            scale = 1 + 0.05 * np.sin(val * PI * 2)
            m.scale(scale / m.pulse_prev_scale)
            m.pulse_prev_scale = scale
            
        battery.pulse_prev_scale = 1.0
        battery.add_updater(pulse_updater)
        
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GREEN)
        self.play(FadeIn(battery))
        self.play(pulse_tracker.animate.set_value(2), run_time=2, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Draw directional arrows (#0000FF) between the blocks during a collision
        # Represent blocks
        block_large = Square(side_length=1.0, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.3)
        block_small = Square(side_length=0.5, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.3)
        
        self.place_at_grid(block_large, "E2", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(block_small, "E5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Momentum Arrow
        arrow = Arrow(start=self.grid["E2"], end=self.grid["E5"], color=BLUE, buff=0.2)
        
        self.lecture[2].set_color(BLUE)
        self.play(FadeIn(block_large), FadeIn(block_small))
        self.play(GrowArrow(arrow))
        
        # Simulate transfer: move arrow or flip it
        arrow_rev = Arrow(start=self.grid["E5"], end=self.grid["E2"], color=BLUE, buff=0.2)
        self.play(Transform(arrow, arrow_rev))
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Clean up updaters
        battery.remove_updater(pulse_updater)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Mapping to Phase Space: The Velocity Vector", [
            "We plot velocities on a two-dimensional graph.",
            "Each point represents the current state of both blocks.",
            "Collisions cause this state point to jump around."
        ])
        
        # Colors
        V1_COLOR = "#0000FF"
        V2_COLOR = "#00FF00"
        POINT_COLOR = "#FFFF00"
        TRAIL_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"
        HIGHLIGHT_COLOR = YELLOW

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        
        # Create axes with colors specified in storyboard
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-2.2, 2.2, 1],
            y_range=[-2.2, 2.2, 1],
            x_length=4,
            y_length=4,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True},
            x_axis_config={"color": V1_COLOR},
            y_axis_config={"color": V2_COLOR}
        )
        x_label = MathTex("v_1", color=V1_COLOR).scale(0.8)
        y_label = MathTex("v_2", color=V2_COLOR).scale(0.8)
        
        # Positioning axes in area B2 to E5 (central part of the right side)
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B2", "E5")
        
        # Position labels near axes tips within 1 unit
        x_label.next_to(axes.x_axis.get_end(), DOWN, buff=0.1)
        y_label.next_to(axes.y_axis.get_end(), LEFT, buff=0.1)
        
        axes_group = VGroup(axes, x_label, y_label)
        self.play(Create(axes_group))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        
        # Initial point at (v1_initial, 0). 
        v1_initial = -1.2
        v2_initial = 0
        point = Dot(axes.c2p(v1_initial, v2_initial), color=POINT_COLOR, radius=0.08)
        
        # The trail follows the point and uses #FFFFFF
        trail = TracedPath(point.get_center, stroke_color=TRAIL_COLOR, stroke_width=2)
        
        # State label that follows the point
        point_label = MathTex("(v_1, v_2)", color=POINT_COLOR).scale(0.7)
        point_label.next_to(point, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        # Keep label centered over the moving point
        point_label.add_updater(lambda d: d.next_to(point, UP, buff=0.1))

        self.add(trail)
        self.play(FadeIn(point), Write(point_label))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        
        # Physics logic for animation visualization (m1=5, m2=1)
        m1, m2 = 5.0, 1.0
        
        def get_next_velocities(v1, v2, type="block"):
            if type == "block":
                # Elastic collision: momentum and energy conservation
                v1_new = ((m1 - m2) / (m1 + m2)) * v1 + (2 * m2 / (m1 + m2)) * v2
                v2_new = (2 * m1 / (m1 + m2)) * v1 - ((m1 - m2) / (m1 + m2)) * v2
                return v1_new, v2_new
            else:
                # Wall hit: v2 flips sign (reflection across X-axis)
                return v1, -v2

        # Step 1: Blocks collide (moves along diagonal)
        v1_1, v2_1 = get_next_velocities(v1_initial, v2_initial, "block")
        self.play(point.animate.move_to(axes.c2p(v1_1, v2_1)), run_time=1.2, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(0.3)
        
        # Step 2: Small block hits wall (instantly reflects across X-axis)
        v1_2, v2_2 = get_next_velocities(v1_1, v2_1, "wall")
        self.play(point.animate.move_to(axes.c2p(v1_2, v2_2)), run_time=0.6, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(0.3)
        
        # Step 3: Blocks collide again
        v1_3, v2_3 = get_next_velocities(v1_2, v2_2, "block")
        self.play(point.animate.move_to(axes.c2p(v1_3, v2_3)), run_time=1.2, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(0.3)

        # Step 4: Wall hit
        v1_4, v2_4 = get_next_velocities(v1_3, v2_3, "wall")
        self.play(point.animate.move_to(axes.c2p(v1_4, v2_4)), run_time=0.6, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Clean up
        point_label.clear_updaters()
        self.play(FadeOut(point_label), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Energy conservation forms an elliptical path on our graph.",
            "We rescale the axes to simplify the geometry.",
            "The ellipse transforms into a perfect, uniform circle.",
            "The system's state now moves along this circular boundary.",
            "Geometry reveals hidden patterns in the block dynamics."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Geometry of Energy: Stretching the Circle", lecture_lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Create coordinate axes for context
        # Using a coordinate system roughly centered in the right-side grid area
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            y_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            x_length=4.5,
            y_length=4.5,
            axis_config={"color": GREY_C},
            tips=False
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'A1', 'F6')
        
        # Ellipse representing the initial energy equation (1/2 M v1^2 + 1/2 m v2^2 = Constant)
        ellipse = Ellipse(width=3.5, height=1.5, color="#00FF00")
        ellipse.move_to(axes.c2p(0, 0))
        
        v1_label = MathTex("v_1", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        v2_label = MathTex("v_2", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(v1_label, 'C6', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(v2_label, 'A3', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Create(axes), Write(v1_label), Write(v2_label))
        self.play(Create(ellipse))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        scaling_x = MathTex(r"\sqrt{M}", font_size=28, color="#00FF00")
        scaling_y = MathTex(r"\sqrt{m}", font_size=28, color="#00FF00")
        
        # Positioning scaling factors near the axes ends
        self.place_at_grid(scaling_x, 'D6', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(scaling_y, 'A4', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Write(scaling_x), Write(scaling_y))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # The transformation to a circle after rescaling the axes
        circle = Circle(radius=1.75, color="#00FFFF")
        circle.move_to(axes.c2p(0, 0))
        
        self.play(
            Transform(ellipse, circle),
            scaling_x.animate.set_color("#00FFFF"),
            scaling_y.animate.set_color("#00FFFF"),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Highlight the perimeter with a glow effect
        # Using a VGroup of circles to simulate a glow
        glow = VGroup(*[
            Circle(radius=1.75 + i*0.05, color="#00FFFF", stroke_width=2).set_opacity(0.3 - i*0.05)
            for i in range(5)
        ])
        glow.move_to(axes.c2p(0, 0))
        
        # A small dot representing the state moving on the circle
        dot = Dot(color=WHITE).move_to(circle.point_from_proportion(0))
        
        self.play(FadeIn(glow))
        self.play(MoveAlongPath(dot, circle), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        self.play(FadeOut(dot))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Fade in the symbol 'Pi' (#FFFF00) at the center of the circle
        pi_sym = MathTex(r"\pi", font_size=72, color="#FFFF00")
        self.place_in_area(pi_sym, 'C3', 'D4')
        
        self.play(FadeIn(pi_sym))
        self.wait(3)
        
        # Final state: reset lecture line color
        self.lecture[4].set_color(WHITE)
        self.wait(1)

        self.play(
            Transform(radial_line2, new_radial_line2),
            Transform(angle_arc, new_angle_arc),
            theta_label.animate.move_to(new_theta_label_pos),
            state_point.animate.move_to(circle.point_at_angle(new_theta)),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)

        # Highlight top half arc
        pi_arc = Arc(radius=2, start_angle=0, angle=PI, arc_center=center, color=WHITE, stroke_width=6)
        
        # We need a label for Pi radians
        pi_label = MathTex(r"\pi \text{ radians}", color=WHITE, font_size=28)

        # Final point traversal to show it fits within Pi

            self.play(
                state_point.animate.move_to(circle.point_at_angle(i * new_theta)),
                run_time=0.2
            )

        self.wait(2)
from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout(
            "Conclusion: The Final Tally", 
            [
                "Larger mass ratios create smaller, more precise angles.",
                "The collision count perfectly matches the digits of Pi.",
                "A surprising link between simple physics and mathematical constants."
            ]
        )
        
        # Colors
        yellow_color = "#FFFF00"
        white_color = "#FFFFFF"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(yellow_color)
        
        # Block simulation visuals
        wall = Line(UP, DOWN, color=white_color).scale(2)
        self.place_at_grid(wall, "C1")
        
        block_m = Square(side_length=0.5, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.5)
        block_M = Square(side_length=1.0, color=RED, fill_opacity=0.5)
        
        self.place_at_grid(block_m, "C2")
        self.place_at_grid(block_M, "C3")
        
        counter_label = Text("Collisions:", font_size=24, color=white_color)
        counter_value = Text("3141", font_size=32, color=yellow_color)
        counter_group = VGroup(counter_label, counter_value).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(counter_group, "B3")
        
        self.play(
            FadeIn(wall),
            FadeIn(block_m),
            FadeIn(block_M),
            FadeIn(counter_group)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(white_color)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(yellow_color)
        
        # Table of mass ratios and counts
        table_header = Text("Mass Ratio | Bounces", font_size=20, color=white_color)
        table_row1 = Text("1 : 1          | 3", font_size=20, color=white_color)
        table_row2 = Text("1 : 100        | 31", font_size=20, color=white_color)
        table_row3 = Text("1 : 10,000     | 314", font_size=20, color=white_color)
        table_row4 = Text("1 : 1,000,000  | 3141", font_size=20, color=white_color)
        
        table = VGroup(table_header, table_row1, table_row2, table_row3, table_row4).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.place_in_area(table, "D2", "F5")
        
        self.play(Write(table))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(white_color)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(yellow_color)
        
        # Fade out everything except collision counter value
        pi_text = Text("π ≈ 3.141...", font_size=48, color=yellow_color)
        self.place_at_grid(pi_text, "C3")
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(wall),
            FadeOut(block_m),
            FadeOut(block_M),
            FadeOut(counter_label),
            FadeOut(table),
            ReplacementTransform(counter_value, pi_text)
        )
        
        self.wait(3)

outline.topic: The Pi Collision Puzzle: Why Counting Bounces Reveals the Universe's Most Famous Constant
outline.target_audience: High school students and undergraduate physics/math enthusiasts

sections.title: The Setup: A Curious Experiment
sections.content: Introduce the physical scenario: A frictionless surface, a wall on the left, and two blocks. A small block sits still, and a much larger block comes charging in from the right. We count every single collision (Block vs. Block and Block vs. Wall).
sections.example: Imagine a giant Elephant-shaped block (Mass M) sliding toward a tiny Ant-shaped block (Mass m). If M = m, there are 3 collisions. If M = 100m, there are 31. If M = 10,000m, there are 314. The digits of Pi appear magically.

sections.title: Prerequisite Knowledge: The Laws of the Game
sections.content: Explain the two fundamental physics principles governing these collisions: Conservation of Energy (the system doesn't lose 'juice') and Conservation of Momentum (the 'push' is transferred). Visualize these as two mathematical equations that must always be satisfied.
sections.example: Use an animation of a pulsing battery icon for 'Energy' and a directional arrow for 'Momentum' to show how they transfer between the Elephant and the Ant during a hit.

sections.title: Mapping to Phase Space: The Velocity Vector
sections.content: Instead of watching the blocks move in space, we plot their velocities on a graph. Let the x-axis be the velocity of the big block (v1) and the y-axis be the velocity of the small block (v2). Every state of the system is just a single point on this graph.
sections.example: Show a 2D coordinate system where the 'state' point moves every time a collision occurs. A wall hit flips the y-coordinate; a block hit moves the point along a specific path.

sections.title: The Geometry of Energy: Stretching the Circle
sections.content: Explain that because Conservation of Energy (1/2 Mv1² + 1/2 mv2² = Constant) looks like the equation of an ellipse, we can 'rescale' the axes by the square root of the masses to turn that ellipse into a perfect circle.
sections.example: An animation showing a squashed oval (ellipse) being physically stretched vertically until it becomes a perfect, glowing circle. The 'state' of our blocks is now a point trapped on the rim of this circle.

sections.title: The Secret Angle: Why Pi?
sections.content: Each collision corresponds to a 'jump' along the arc of this circle. Because of the mass ratio, each jump covers a tiny, constant angle. We count how many jumps it takes to go halfway around the circle (180 degrees or Pi radians) before the blocks move away from each other forever.
sections.example: Visualize the circle as a clock face. Each collision is a 'tick' of the hand. As the mass of the Elephant increases, the 'tick' becomes smaller, requiring more hits to traverse the Pi-arc of the circle.

sections.title: Conclusion: The Final Tally
sections.content: Summarize how the number of collisions is the integer part of (Pi / angle). As the mass ratio becomes a power of 100, the angle becomes perfectly aligned with the decimal positions of Pi.
sections.example: A final high-speed montage: M = 1,000,000m. The counter blurs as the blocks vibrate, finally stopping at exactly 3,141. The screen overlays the digits of Pi over the block counter.
